Rambunctious

ram-BUHNK-shuhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Rambunctious is uncontrollably rowdy, boisterous, or full of unruly energy.

The rambunctious crowd at the block party spilled out into the street long after the official festivities had ended.

Worked Example

The rambunctious golden retriever puppy flattened three houseplants and a stack of mail before breakfast was even over.

The puppy wasn't being deliberately destructive; it was simply bursting with uncontrolled energy, which is what makes behavior rambunctious rather than just naughty.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rambunc-

root — rambunc-: origin uncertain -- likely a 19th-century American alteration of the older word rumbustious (uncertain, American English)

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Rambunctious's exact origin is genuinely murky -- most dictionaries treat it as an American alteration of the older British word rumbustious, itself of uncertain origin. It still behaves like a normal -ious adjective (full of rowdy energy); it just doesn't peel apart into a tidy, reusable root.

Use the root in a new word: rumbustious

Use the root in a new word: rumbustious: The Victorian critic dismissed the play as a rumbustious mess of shouting and slapstick.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Rambunctious almost always describes children, young animals, or lively crowds -- energy that's more endearing than threatening.
